title: Velaire — WebMCP Agreements for Service Businesses
pitch: Two independent agents negotiate through a live service website while humans control every consequential decision—with versioned offers, immutable receipts, and accountable change orders.
about_excerpt: Two independent agents negotiate through a live service website while humans control every consequential decision—with versioned offers, immutable receipts, and accountable change orders. Like Comment Story Updates System architecture: two independent ChatGPT agents share one revisioned ServiceCase while humans retain final authority. Live sequence: request, evidence, offer, counter, revision, booking and acknowledgment across separate agent sessions. Owner journey: scan the queue, read the case, stage terms, visibly send, wait for the customer and propose changed work. Customer journey: qualify, verify, open a case, negotiate, compare versions and prepare a human-confirmed booking. WebMCP observability exposes result codes, latency, revision effects, recovery states and zero autonomous commitments. Promise diff: offer V1, customer counter, accepted V2 and later changed work stay visible against the frozen receipt. Safety and trust gates cover emergencies, privacy, state, revisions, offers, human approval, asynchronous waits and audit. Structured tool results become useful map, route, market-price, project-timeline and agreement artifacts for people. WebMCP tool surface for discovery, evidence, negotiation, booking, routing, project planning, change control and audit. Evidence-aware discovery uses provenance, freshness, synthetic labels and untrusted-content hints before recommending a next step. Native WebMCP replaces brittle click automation with declared intent, typed inputs, explicit effects and valid next actions. Agreement state machine: valid states, revision checks and visible human gates control every consequential transition. Recorded proof: both sides finish on revision 9, a $320 authorized total and the same append-only decision trail. Recorded proof: the customer agent opens a request and the independent owner agent retrieves the same case and constraints. Recorded proof: a +$145 change order stays pending beside the locked $175 booking until the customer decides. Inspiration Service businesses already have websites, but most of those sites expose pages and contact forms rather than the structured truth an AI agent needs to complete a real customer journey. Pricing, availability, exclusions, messages, approvals, and later change orders are scattered across interfaces. An agent can discover a business yet still over-promise, act on stale terms, or mistake a private draft for an accepted agreement. We built Velaire to test a more useful WebMCP pattern: can an ordinary service website become a trustworthy agreement room for a customer's agent, an owner's agent, and the two humans who retain authority? What it does Velaire is a WebMCP-native reference implementation for service businesses, demonstrated through a fictional HVAC company. A customer speaks naturally to ChatGPT; the live website publishes typed capabilities that let the agent check service fit, policies, business evidence, pricing, and safety before opening a structured service case. A separate owner ChatGPT finds that same case through the owner route. The agents are independent and never role-play both parties in one conversation. They communicate through one revisioned ServiceCase that remains authoritative for messages, offers, counters, bookings, receipts, and changed work. The owner agent may prepare an offer, but it stays private until the owner presses Send. The customer agent may compare versions and prepare a booking, but only the customer can confirm it. That confirmation freezes an immutable receipt. If work changes later, Velaire compares the proposed charge against the exact accepted snapshot instead of silently rewriting history. Demo journey The customer asks for same-day help with an AC blowing warm air. ChatGPT checks eligibility, pricing evidence, availability, credentials, and safety. It opens a case with a $180 ceiling and explicit no-surprise-fee constraints. A separate owner agent retrieves the live request and prepares a $195 offer. The owner visibly sends the offer. The customer counters at $175 with no travel or after-hours fee. The owner sends offer version two. The customer agent compares both versions field by field. The agent prepares the booking; the customer confirms it, creating an immutable $175 receipt. The owner proposes a +$145 capacitor change order. Velaire shows the added scope, $320 total, and time impact against the original promise. The customer approves the change, the owner acknowledges it, and both agents independently read revision 9 with no pending decision. No real payment is taken, and every person, address, credential, review, price, and transaction shown is synthetic demonstration data. The WebMCP tool surface Customer discovery and trust velaire_check_service_fit checks need, postcode, urgency, budget, safety, and service eligibility. velaire_get_business_evidence returns source cards for credentials, pricing, availability, cancellation, warranty, and reviews. velaire_get_market_price_context and velaire_compare_quote_context provide transparent pricing context without presenting synthetic estimates as live market truth. Service, policy, site-search, contact, and agent-help tools make the ordinary website understandable without scraping its buttons. Shared customer–owner workflow velaire_open_service_case creates the authoritative record. velaire_get_service_case returns its current revision, messages, offers, decisions, and valid next actions. velaire_submit_case_message adds a bounded question or counteroffer and rejects stale revisions. velaire_wait_for_owner_reply and velaire_wait_for_customer_reply represent waiting honestly, with timeout and cancellation recovery. velaire_set_service_location, velaire_plan_service_route, and velaire_get_case_visuals return map, route, timeline, and visual artifacts. Owner workflow velaire_list_service_cases and velaire_get_owner_case expose the owner queue and exact case state. velaire_stage_owner_reply, velaire_stage_service_offer, and velaire_stage_change_order keep drafts private until a visible human Send action. Agreement protection and audit velaire_compare_offer_versions compares price, timing, deposit, warranty, scope, exclusions, and expiry deterministically. velaire_prepare_booking stages one exact offer version; it cannot confirm it. velaire_get_booking_receipt returns the full accepted snapshot rather than a mutable offer reference. velaire_compare_change_order checks later work against the accepted promise. velaire_audit_invoice_against_receipt detects invoice drift. velaire_get_webmcp_health exposes tool-call success, latency, revisions, read/action distribution, and recovery states. How we built it Velaire uses React, strict TypeScript, and Vite, deployed as a static application on Vercel. It registers native imperative tools through document.modelContext.registerTool(). video_transcript_excerpt: This walk through uses the AI voice of a mod Bukhari. The lair is a normal service business website. It's live page also gives a customer's chat GPT a structured way to understand the business and take safe action without scraping buttons or guessing from page text. The customer says the air conditioner is blowing warm air and asks for same-day help. Chat GPT checks service area, pricing, availability, credentials, and safety, then opens a case. The customer never needs a tool name. The owner's separate chat GPT checks the live queue and finds that case. Two independent agents in two independent sessions now communicate through one authoritative service record. The owner's agent prepares a response, but the draft stays private until the owner presses send. The first offer is $195 with a 2:00 to 4:00 p.m. window and a $49 deposit. The customer counters at 175 with no travel or after-hours fee. The owner sees that revision and sends a new offer. Now the customer's agent compares both versions field by field. It confirms the $20 reduction and checks that the schedule, deposit, warranty, scope, and exclusions have not quietly become worse. Chat GPT prepares the booking, but cannot accept it. The terms stay visibly pending until the customer confirms them on the page. That human action creates an immutable receipt for the accepted $175 agreement. No payment is taken. Next, the owner discovers a weak capacitor and proposes a $145 change order. The agreement is not overwritten. The customer sees added scope, total, and schedule impact against the accepted snapshot, then chooses whether to approve it. After approval, the authorized total is $320. The owner sends a final acknowledgement and both sides independently read the same revision with no pending decision. What you just saw is a chain of purpose-built web MCP tools. On the customer side, service fit and business evidence tools checked eligibility, pricing, source cards, and safety. Case and reply waiting tools carried the conversation without scraping the page. On the owner side, Q reply, offer, and change order tools kept every draft private until the owner pressed send. Comparison, booking preparation, receipt, map, route, and market price tools then gave the customer verifiable artifacts instead of a vague "Okay." The audit and health tools expose every call, revision, outcome, and latency. More importantly, the missing layer we address is not another chatbot. It is safe, asynchronous, two-party agreement infrastructure for service websites. Structured negotiation, explicit human consent, immutable receipts, and later charges compared against the promise that was actually accepted. HVAC is the reference implementation, but the same pattern can serve any service business.

live_observation.first_impression: A polished HVAC service landing page offering agent-assisted service and a human request path, with transparent-policy source cards.
live_observation.after_state: The click completed without a confirmed booking or visible outcome in the captured state.
